title: Route-resolution contract checker with progressive schema hardening
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Replace the brittle ad-hoc routing rule checks with a deterministic route-resolution contract checker that validates DSL configs incrementally and provides actionable errors and automated migrations.

Scope:
- Design a typed contract for routing resolution that includes region selectors, tier priorities, model variant fallbacks, and cost/latency hints.
- Implement a validator that runs at config-apply time and emits machine-readable errors and suggested fixes.
- Support staged hardening: allow "soft" warnings initially, escalate to errors after a rollout window.
- Provide a migration tool that rewrites legacy rule snippets into the new canonical shape where safe.
- Integrate fuzz tests and property-based checks to catch ambiguous fallback loops and unintended region exclusion.

Non-goals: reworking the runtime router or scheduling heuristics (this ticket provides the contracts and tests the config surface only).

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Use a small typed AST for the DSL to keep validation deterministic; avoid full Turing-complete evaluation inside the validator. This trades some expressivity for testability and safety.
- Progressive enforcement: configs are annotated with a policy-version and enforcement-level. During rollout we will emit warnings to the Console audit stream and only transition to strict enforcement after one week and QA sign-off.
- Migration: automated rewrites will be conservative (idempotent on safe patterns). For ambiguous cases the tool will create a migration PR with the suggested change and link to the failing rule.

Acceptance criteria:
- New validator binary (policy-contract-check) runs as a pre-apply hook and in CI, with <150ms median runtime on typical org config (100 rules).
- Validator produces stable error codes (RFC-style) and a suggestion payload string for automated fixes.
- Migration tool can successfully rewrite >80% of legacy region-tier fallback patterns in our config corpus with zero behavioral delta on unit tests.
- End-to-end integration: Console shows warnings for soft-enforced rules; warning-to-error transition is gated by a release flag.

Test plan: unit tests for AST, property-based fuzzing for fallback graphs, integration tests with a config corpus (we will snapshot 200 recent active configs), and end-to-end rollout simulation in staging.

Monitoring & observability: invalid config counts and their error codes will be recorded in the infra metrics table (policy.validator.errors) and surfaced on a new Console card. We will also log migration PR outcomes for tracking regressions.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: scoped the typed AST and enforcement levels. Agreement to keep validator pure (no network calls).
2025-02-20 - Architecture review notes: PM requested a migration-first approach; ops asked for slow rollout via soft warnings. Added enforcement-level field.

2025-02-26 - Proto impl: initial AST and parser landed in branch feature/ENG-100207-ast. Parser passes round-trip tests against 120 sample rules. GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2158
2025-03-01 - QA feedback: found a fallback loop case where two variants circularly prefer each other under region weight ties. Added graph-cycle detection to validator.
2025-03-03 - Security review queued. Reused KMS audit pattern; security asked for a config redaction step in migration PRs to avoid including sensitive customer labels.
